hypotheses.reasoning: order-consumer is crash-looping on a single message, msg-329298 at offset 442796 on orders.events. Every restart fails on the same offset with RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded in expandReferences (#735, #755, #778). The process exits with code 1 and restarts with growing backoff (#737, #757, #782). Because the consumer never commits past this offset, it cannot advance, which explains the rising orders.events lag. The message is likely malformed, for example a self-referencing or deeply nested reference structure that makes the recursive expandReferences overflow. Before the crash the consumer was healthy, processing batches with low lag (#730 and earlier). The report-cron ModuleNotFoundError for pandas (image report-cron:2026.10.2) is a separate fault that does not touch order-consumer, and the order-service, payment-svc, api-gateway, redis and postgres logs show no errors. I did not pull the message payload itself, so the malformation is inferred from the stack overflow rather than confirmed.

The report-cron image 2026.10.2 is missing the pandas module and fails every run. This is a real and separate defect, but it does not affect order-consumer and cannot explain the consumer crash loop. Listed only as a ruled-out alternative.

verdict.recommendedAction: Skip or dead-letter offset 442796 (msg-329298) on orders.events, or move it to a DLQ, so order-consumer can advance past it. Then inspect that payload for circular or deeply nested references and fix expandReferences to handle them, or add a depth guard. Separately, fix report-cron:2026.10.2 by adding the pandas dependency to its image or rolling back to the previous image. That is a separate issue from h-023.
